messages.text: Humphries dazzles on the doubles to reach Grand Prix quarter-finals

metadata.summary: Luke Humphries put in a much-improved display as his doubling prowess and a 10-dart finish secured a 3-0 rout of Jermaine Wattimena and a spot in the World Grand Prix quarter-finals.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade storm into quarter-finals as Gary Anderson eliminated | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade storm into quarter-finals as Gary Anderson eliminated Luke Humphries goes at 74 per cent on his starting doubles and 64 per cent on his closing ones as he sweeps Jermaine Wattimena 3-0, will face Niels Zonneveld in last eight after Dutch debutant dispatches Gary Anderson; James Wade excels against Stephen Bunting Friday 2 October 2026 00:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries fired in a 10-dart finish as he swept Jermaine Wattimena aside at the World Grand Prix Luke Humphries put in a much-improved display as his doubling prowess and a 10-dart finish secured a 3-0 rout of Jermaine Wattimena and a spot in the World Grand Prix quarter-finals. There were also 3-1 victories for James Wade and Niels Zonneveld over Stephen Bunting and Gary Anderson respectively, while Gian Van Veen came through a deciding-set cracker with Ryan Searle to triumph 3-2. Humphries - the title favourite after defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night - had averaged only 80 and gone at 26 per cent on his closing doubles in a scruffy 2-0 win over Dave Chisnall on Tuesday evening. messages.text: HMRC asked to explore tax implications of Man City case

metadata.summary: The Treasury Committee has written to the chief executive of HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to ask about the tax implications of the Premier League's investigation into Manchester City.
metadata.content: Man City charges: Treasury Committee writes to HMRC to ask about tax implications of Premier League investigation | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: Treasury Committee writes to HMRC to ask about tax implications of Premier League investigation Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday to do so Thursday 1 October 2026 20:01, UK Image: An aerial view over the Etihad Stadium in Manchester The Treasury Committee has written to the chief executive of HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to ask about the tax implications of the Premier League's investigation into Manchester City. HMRC could investigate whether City paid the right amount of tax and national insurance during the nine seasons they have been found guilty of financial rule breaches. In the letter, Dame Meg Hillier MP asks JP Marks, permanent secretary of HMRC, whether the department has received an unredacted version of the Premier League's report and requests "reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case".
